observations: Line 2 uses a raw string prefix check `resolved.startswith(root)` rather than a path-component boundary check.

Probe p1 `permitted('/srv/app', '/srv/application/key')` returns True because '/srv/application/key' starts with '/srv/app', violating the stated contract that only root and its descendants are allowed.
Probe p2 `permitted('/srv/app', '/srv/app/file')` returns True, consistent with the contract.
The function performs no normalization or separator handling; correctness depends entirely on the caller honoring the stated precondition of canonical absolute POSIX paths without trailing slash.
No exception handling is present; non-string or None inputs would raise AttributeError at line 2 rather than being rejected.
The changed line is the sole authorization decision point, so the prefix-boundary weakness is the entire enforcement surface.
